chunks: We used to sit in places to listen to it; but whoever listens now will find a shooting star in wait for him.
ai.seo_question: Why did jinn use to sit in specific places to listen to the heavens?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the transition in cosmic governance where jinn, who previously eavesdropped on the heavens to gather news, now face expulsion by shooting stars (shihab) upon attempting to listen. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, interpret this as a sign of the sealing of revelation or the increased vigilance of angels, emphasizing the shift from the pre-Islamic era to the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
